drafted_from: tool:github:danielgatis-rembg's row in tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json (job, run, get_it, needs) and its sources row in sources.json; the command is the row's own run line with synthetic names filled in. What it prints or writes is read from the tool's documented behavior; the folder test test/index-github-tools.test.mjs only checks the row, never runs rembg.
start_here: Say to your AI: "Use rembg on my computer to remove the background from an image to make a cutout with a transparent background: the file is loaf.jpg." It reads the row, installs rembg if it is missing, runs it on that one file and shows you what it made.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: rembg is a program that runs on the person's own computer and works on the one file or address it is handed.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Use rembg on loaf.jpg". It reads the row with run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools, method tools:list, input {tool: "tool:github:danielgatis-rembg"}.
2. It checks that python are on your computer, and if rembg is missing it runs the get_it steps: git clone https://github.com/danielgatis/rembg.git ; pip install "rembg[cpu,cli]".
3. It runs the row's command with your file in place of {input} and where the result goes in place of {output}: rembg i loaf.jpg loaf-cutout.png
4. Read what it shows you and open the result. Trillion runs none of this; it all happens on your own computer.

worked_examples.title: rembg on a product photo of a loaf of bread on a kitchen table
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json: tool:github:danielgatis-rembg runs on your computer, so after tools:list the AI runs, in the folder it got rembg in, the command line: rembg i loaf.jpg loaf-cutout.png  (synthetic input: a product photo of a loaf of bread on a kitchen table).
worked_examples.hands_back: rembg prints nothing and writes loaf-cutout.png: the same loaf with the table and kitchen removed, on a transparent background.
